output.summary: The yield decline is real: gauge R&R is stable, the CMM program and reject criteria are unchanged, and the definition is unchanged. New operators are not worse than experienced ones, and yield fell before they ran alone, so H4 is contradicted. Four changes overlap in time: 12-hour shifts, the Corvane steel, the deferred spindle service and rising hardness spread. L3-02 and L3-05 have worse runout, but they also run the tighter-tolerance long shaft, so R2 is only an association. The scrap-tag timing is a recording artifact, so fatigue is unestablished. The deferral of the service was driven by backlog pressure. The causes cannot be separated without the Line 6 spare lathe CMM data or a staggered service with Tamsworth trial lots (A2). Punishing operators or cutting inspection would be harmful.
